subject: Benchmark methodology & runbook — SLO targets, streaming, and reproducibility
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Samantha Lee <samantha@clearbuy.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.ai>, Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-10-20T15:12:00-07:00
Subject: Benchmark methodology & runbook — follow-up and next steps

Hi Samantha —

Thanks for a productive discovery this morning. Quick recap and the things we promised to follow up on: 

- ClearBuy targets you called out: p50 generation latency <= 100 ms, p95 <= 300 ms for non-streaming requests, sustained throughput target ~120 req/s, and target concurrency of ~40 simultaneous inference sessions. For streaming scenarios you indicated a hard requirement of <200 ms per-token tail latency at 50 concurrent streams.
- You have a set of representative prompt families and a sampling of user sessions we can use for the qualification harness.
- You requested a reproducible runbook and a clear measurement spec so procurement can sign off on the SLOs.

Attached is a first draft of a latency runbook I referenced during the call (latency_runbook_draft.md). Can you attach the prompt samples + any ground-truth expectations you have (pass/fail criteria per prompt family) — that will let our benchmarking team configure the harness exactly the way ClearBuy needs it.

Proposed next steps: 
1) Samantha to send prompt samples + SOC2 scope doc (if available) — due by EOD Thu 10/22
2) Redwood to produce a reproducible benchmark plan and an estimated runtime + ticketed artifacts by Mon 10/26
3) Schedule a short (30m) calibration call the week of 10/26 to agree on measurement windows and traffic shaping.

If those timelines look good I'll loop in engineering and set the calendar invites.

Thanks again — excited to move this to qualification.

—Marissa

From: Samantha Lee <samantha@clearbuy.com>

Cc: Tom Harper <tom.harper@clearbuy.com>, ClearBuy Procurement <procurement@clearbuy.com>
Date: 2026-10-21T09:04:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Benchmark methodology & runbook — follow-up and next steps

Marissa —

Thanks for the recap. Attaching the prompt samples you requested (clearbuy_prompt_samples_v1.csv) and our SOC2 scope summary for reference. A few clarifications from our side to make the measurement plan actionable: 

- Prompt mix: 60% short transactional prompts (user intent extraction), 25% medium (50–150 token generation), 15% long/contextual (>=250 token contexts). Please preserve the grouping in the CSV so metrics can be segmented.
- Test traffic: please run both a steady-state run (120 req/s target for 30 minutes) and a burst run (200 req/s sustained for 2 minutes, then back to steady).
- Concurrency model: we use long-lived sessions for streaming; for streaming qualification please emulate 50 concurrent streams with average keypress-driven token bursts (token bursts of 1–5 tokens every ~200–500 ms).
- Measurement definitions: define tail latencies at p95 and p99 for both generation and token-streaming endpoints. For streaming token latency measure the 95th percentile of per-token emission latency (time from model-ready to token delivered).
- Pass/fail criteria: 
  * Non-streaming: p95 <= 300 ms and p50 <= 100 ms across all prompt families
  * Streaming: p95 per-token latency <= 200 ms with <1% dropped streams during the run

We can be flexible on model variants — we want to see a baseline model and a quantized 4-bit variant if possible. Also include a note on reproducibility: record seeds, model versions, hardware SKU, and network egress/ingress conditions in the run artifacts.

We'll review your runbook and should be able to signoff on the measurement spec as long as the harness can reproduce the traffic shape above.

Thanks — attaching files now.

—Samantha
Samantha Lee
Senior ML Platform Manager | ClearBuy
samantha@clearbuy.com

Attachments: clearbuy_prompt_samples_v1.csv (CSV, 42 KB); clearbuy_soc2_scope.pdf (PDF, 120 KB)

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Samantha Lee <samantha@clearbuy.com>
Cc: Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.ai>, Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-10-22T11:38:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Benchmark methodology & runbook — follow-up and next steps

Looping in Grace (benchmark lead) and Kim (solutions eng) to draft a reproducible benchmark and clarify a few engineering constraints. Early notes from infra/bench team: 

- We'll run on two variants as requested: baseline FP16 and quantized 4-bit (same architecture). We'll include model hashes and exact runner versions in the artifact manifest.
- Proposed harness runs: 
  1) Warmup + steady-state: 10m warmup, 30m steady at 120 req/s segmented by prompt family\  
  2) Burst window: repeat 3x: 2-minute 200 req/s burst followed by 8-minute cooldown\  
  3) Streaming stability: 45–60 minute streaming run with 50 concurrent streams, record per-token latencies and stream-drop events
- Measurement tooling: we'll publish artifacts including raw event logs, per-request timing (client and server), and a reproducibility README (seeds, environment variables, hardware SKU, kernel versions, load generator commit).
- Network: to match your environment we will run tests from our us-west region with an optional egress shaping step to simulate your office-to-cloud RTT if you provide a target RTT distribution.

Grace and Kim — please confirm you can produce the reproducibility README and a minimal Jupyter notebook to re-run the analysis. Samantha — is there any additional constraint on acceptable hardware (e.g., no preemptible GPUs)? Also confirming procurement wants the final measurement spec in a format they can attach to the PO (PDF).

If everyone is aligned I'll schedule the calibration call for Thu 10/29 and start the runbook draft for review.

Thanks,
Ben
Principal Solutions Architect | Redwood Inference
ben.carter@redwood.ai

Subject: Re: Benchmark methodology & runbook — follow-up and next steps

Ben/Grace/Kim —

This plan looks good to us. A few confirmations before the calibration call: 

- No preemptible GPUs, please. Procurement requires dedicated instances for the qualification runs.
- Include an explicit artifact that states the version of the compiler/kernels used (we'll need this for auditability).
- For the streaming stability run, please log token-level timestamps and the client-side clock skew so we can independently verify per-token latency.

We can do the calibration call on Thu 10/29 at 10:00 AM PT. I can bring Tom from infra and a procurement rep if needed. Once the runbook is finalized and we see a dry-run summary, we'll attach the measurement spec PDF to the PO and proceed to sign-off.

Looking forward to the calibration.

—Samantha
